title: DialectProfile
description: One dialect's execution facts as data: what the engine can and cannot do, how its own error messages become the closed QueryResult codes, how a stored value becomes a JSON cell, and which affinity a declared type selects. contracts/dialects/<dialect>.json is the profile both the Go gateway and the browser adapter read; this schema is the shape the audit (scripts/sqlite-error-codes.mjs) validates it against. `dialect` and `engine` are a closed set whose members are exactly the profiles present under contracts/dialects/.

engine_label.description: How the engine names itself to a learner, e.g. "SQLite 3.x". A label, never a version guarantee.

capabilities.description: One boolean per dialect capability. Every key must have a non-empty note in capability_notes, and capability_notes may key nothing that is not here; the audit checks the two key sets match.

capability_notes.description: The reason for each capability's value. A capability with no note is a claim without a source.

error_classification.description: The ordered, first-match-wins message-to-code table. An empty `contains` pattern in the last rule is the catch-all; the audit fails if anything follows it.

source.description: The human-facing document this profile is the machine-readable half of.

dialectName.description: The dialects with a profile under contracts/dialects/ — one member per file. The audit fails if this set and the files on disk disagree.

queryResultErrorCode.description: The closed QueryResult error enum, copied in contract order from contracts/query-result.schema.json. The audit fails if the two enums ever differ, so a profile cannot name a code outside the contract.

match.description: How `pattern` is tested against the engine's message.

pattern.description: The message test. An empty pattern under `contains` matches every message and is the catch-all.

note.description: Which engine result code this is, and why the contract code is the correct one.

affinityClass.description: SQLite's five affinity classes, in the order the engine's algorithm lists them.

when.description: The declared-type test that selects this affinity.

affinity_rules.description: The affinity algorithm in the order the engine applies it, first match wins.

declared.description: Each declared type this dataset uses, mapped to the one affinity class it selects.

jsonKind.description: A JSON value kind — the only things a QueryResult cell can be.

rule.description: The encoding rule in one line.

note.description: Why this rule is the honest one.

valueEncoding.description: One rule per SQLite storage class — NULL, INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB — plus the cases where a driver materialises a value the engine never stored a class for. The declared affinity of the column does not change any of them.
